items.why: Course catalogue entry swapped and review/rating counters ticked up; no pricing change.
A $5.99 per user per month figure appeared in the on-demand (pay as you go) AI text for the first time; unclear what it bills, so not treated as a change to an existing price.
Two-year Advanced and Express Pro first-28-month totals dropped (USD$126 → USD$117.32, USD$210 → USD$201.32); Basic moved by a few cents.

record.short: Advanced 2-year plan first 28 months USD$126 → USD$117.32; Express Pro USD$210 → USD$201.32.
record.headline: ExpressVPN lowered the promotional first-28-month price of its Advanced and Express Pro 2-year plans, with Basic barely changed.
record.who: New customers buying the 2-year plans; the renewal prices shown (USD$99.95, USD$119.95, USD$199.95 annually) are unchanged.
record.read: Looks like a deeper promotional discount on the two upper tiers, steering buyers away from Basic. Likely a seasonal promotion rather than a list-price reset, though that is an inference.
record.caveat: Per-month display moved from fractions (e.g. USD$4½) to decimals (USD$4.19); promotional first-term prices only.

items.why: Existing 50%-off-for-3-months promo only had its date window shifted by one day.
Page served two versions in one run: old Managed/Expert Service packages and a new Pro/Premium layout at the same $249/$299 with different bundled services (looks like a test).

record.short: Managed Service $249 → Pro $249 and Expert Service $299 → Premium $299, with different bundled services.
record.headline: LegalZoom is showing some visitors a repackaged LLC formation lineup where the two paid packages keep their prices but swap the bundled services.
record.who: New LLC formation buyers who are shown the new layout; not clear how many visitors see it.
record.read: The new top package drops the accountant, tax-prep and always-on team service in favour of bookkeeping software, which lowers the recurring fee after the trial. Because both versions appeared in the same run, this is an A/B test, not a decided change.
record.caveat: Unstable page: both versions were served within the same run. The phone number and many copy details also differ.

items.why: Enterprise button changed from Request demo to Talk to sales and feature line breaks reflowed; no price or limit change.
Page flipped between CAD and USD rendering (CA$37 vs $44 etc.) with feature-list reordering; a currency/region rendering difference, not a price change.
FAQ definition of an AI conversation expanded; the 500 conversations per month allowance is unchanged.
A Model APIs per-token rate card was added; no existing price changed.
Intermediate plan changed from Unlimited Posts to a cap of 800 Scheduled Posts.

record.short: Intermediate plan posts: Unlimited → 800 scheduled posts, price unchanged at $48 and $60.

items.why: Model list in the plan copy updated (Smaug + DeepSeek replaced by DeepSeek v4.1 + Kimi K3.1 Pro); no price or limit change.
A help prompt (Need help finding the right Plaud?) was removed; no pricing change.
Credits FAQ was rewritten and split into a table, with the same $18 per seat credits and the same $2 one-time free credits; no price or limit change.
